query: What does Claudette's behavior suggest about her stance on development and change on Maple Street?
gold: Claudette consistently opposes any planning application that would alter the street's residential character. In Session 1, her immediate response to the no. 22 loft conversion notice was 'This street does not need any more bulk added to it. I shall be objecting.' She frames this in terms of visual impact and preserving the street's character — not noise, not traffic. In Session 3, she linked the traffic danger Marcus experienced to development ('All this traffic is exactly what happens when you allow more development'). Her thirty-year tenure gives her a before-and-after frame that shapes all of her planning opinions.
context:
[1] (about=Claudette, episodic, t4 @2025-05-19T09:02:00) How frightening. I remember when this was a quiet road. All this traffic is exactly what happens when you allow more development, more occupants, more cars, more danger for our children.
[2] (about=Claudette, episodic, t0 @2025-05-05T11:17:00) I saw it this morning. I remember when no. 22 was a single-storey cottage. This street does not need any more bulk added to it. I shall be objecting.
agent_answer: Claudette’s behavior suggests she is opposed to development and change on Maple Street. She recalls when the street was quiet, describes added traffic and occupants as dangerous for children, and says the street “does not need any more bulk added to it”—stating she will object to the development.
